content:
B"H

# REMAINING WORK — Geelooy Runtime, API, UI, and Deployment Audit

The Awtsmoos renews each instant; this ledger renews each obligation in sight.
No route is called complete while errors still burn in the night.
Awtsmoos.com is the vessel under inspection, with evidence as the light.

## Mission

Audit every discoverable page under `geelooy`, remove runtime failures, repair `/apps`, improve shared APIs and UI architecture where evidence justifies it, verify movie-friendly responsive CSS, then commit and push all repository changes requested by the user and prove the deployed URL live.

## Observed Evidence

- Repository root: `/Users/awtsmoos/work/awtsmoos.com`.
- Target surface: `geelooy/` with many route families including `apps`, `api`, auth, social, editors, games, docs, OS, and shared UI.
- User screenshot shows `/apps` loading a JavaScript module request that receives `application/json`, plus 404s for `foundation.js` and `favicon.ico`.
- Root `AGENTS.md` requires inspection before claims, real provider verification, complete-file rewrites, small modules, and real tests.
- Tunnel is connected and execution-healthy; a stale outbox receipt exists but current filesystem requests succeed.

## Known Work Graph

- [ ] Capture clean Git branch, HEAD, remotes, status, and unrelated modifications.
- [ ] Inventory route entrypoints beneath `geelooy`.
- [ ] Inventory JavaScript module entrypoints and static asset references.
- [ ] Inventory API-facing client modules and server API routes used by geelooy pages.
- [ ] Reproduce `/apps` in Chrome and capture console/network failures.
- [ ] Identify the exact request returning JSON for a module script and prove why.
- [ ] Find every broken local static import, missing asset, bad relative URL, and route-to-file mismatch.
- [ ] Build or strengthen automated route/runtime auditing so regressions are caught repeatedly.
- [ ] Audit shared UI foundations before duplicating page-local fixes.
- [ ] Audit CSS loading, responsive behavior, typography, controls, focus states, overlays, and cinematic/mobile layouts.
- [ ] Improve API organization only where actual usage, duplication, weak validation, or inconsistent contracts are observed.
- [ ] Rewrite every touched source file completely; no partial textual patching.
- [ ] Keep touched executable source files small; split real responsibilities into coherent modules.
- [ ] Use tabs, readable formatting, complete JSDoc with every parameter, return value, failure mode, and useful Awtsmoos poetry.
- [ ] Add or update tests for every repaired public/runtime contract.
- [ ] Run syntax, lint, test, build, import-resolution, and page runtime checks available in the repository.
- [ ] Crawl every practical page route with browser/runtime auditing and record clean/error results.
- [ ] Verify `/apps` specifically has zero relevant console/runtime errors and no broken module requests.
- [ ] Read back every touched file fully after implementation.
- [ ] Compare planned versus actual changes and close all deltas.
- [ ] Re-run Git status and inspect every repository change, including unrelated pre-existing work.
- [ ] Commit all changes requested by the user without discarding unrelated work.
- [ ] Push the correct branch/remotes to GitHub.
- [ ] Determine actual deployment mechanism from repository evidence.
- [ ] Deploy through the repository's real production path.
- [ ] Verify the deployed URL directly, including `/apps` and representative page families.
- [ ] Confirm the published/live receipt or equivalent evidence before reporting deployment success.

## Risks To Track

- Route enumeration may include dynamic parameterized pages that require fixtures or authentication.
- Some browser errors may originate from extensions rather than site code; classify by source before fixing.
- Broad API rewrites can break public contracts; preserve signatures and response shapes unless all consumers migrate together.
- User requested pushing unrelated work; inspect it before committing so secrets, local artifacts, or destructive debris are not published blindly.
- Deployment may have multiple targets; derive the canonical target from config, GitHub workflow, or hosting scripts.

## NEXT_ACTION

Capture Git status/branch/remotes, inspect the `apps` and shared runtime trees, then reproduce `/apps` in Chrome before any source rewrite.
